This vignette covers the overlay family — dialog, sheet, drawer, alert-dialog —
and the server-side helpers that open them and raise toasts.

## Trigger-driven vs server-driven

Every overlay accepts a `trigger`: a UI element that opens it on click. Give the
overlay an `inputId` and its open state is reported as a logical `input$id`.

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(shadshiny)

shad_dialog(
  "settings",
  trigger = shad_button("Settings", variant = "outline"),
  title = "Settings",
  shad_input("name", label = "Display name"),
  footer = shad_dialog_close_button("Done")
)
```

The same overlay can be opened (or closed) from the server without any trigger,
using `shad_dialog_open()` / `shad_dialog_close()`. Each overlay has a matching
pair — `shad_sheet_open()`, `shad_drawer_open()`, `shad_alert_dialog_open()`,
`shad_popover_open()`, and so on.

```{r}
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$launch, {
    shad_dialog_open("settings")
  })
  observeEvent(input$settings, {
    # TRUE when open, FALSE when dismissed
    message("settings dialog open? ", input$settings)
  })
}
```

## Confirm flows with alert-dialog

`shad_alert_dialog()` is the modal-confirmation pattern. Its action button is a
Shiny action button with id `<inputId>_confirm`, so you observe the confirm the
same way you observe any action button:

```{r}
ui <- shad_alert_dialog(
  "wipe",
  trigger = shad_button("Delete account", variant = "destructive"),
  title = "Delete your account?",
  description = "This cannot be undone.",
  cancel = "Keep it",
  action = "Delete",
  action_variant = "destructive"
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$wipe_confirm, {
    # user pressed the destructive action
    shad_toast_success("Account deleted.")
  })
}
```

## Toasts

Toasts are server-only notifications. `shad_toast()` takes a message plus
`title`, `description`, `variant`, and `duration`; the shorthands
`shad_toast_success()`, `shad_toast_error()`, `shad_toast_warning()`, and
`shad_toast_loading()` set the variant for you.

```{r}
shad_toast_success("Saved", description = "Your changes are live.")
shad_toast_error("Upload failed", description = "Check your connection.")
```

### Loading → done

`shad_toast_loading()` shows an indefinite spinner and returns an id. Feed that
id to `shad_toast_update()` when the work finishes to morph the same toast into
a result — no second toast, no flicker.

```{r}
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$export, {
    id <- shad_toast_loading("Exporting…")
    later::later(function() {
      shad_toast_update(id, variant = "success",
                        message = "Export ready")
    }, delay = 2)
  })
}
```

Dismiss programmatically with `shad_toast_dismiss(id)`, or
`shad_toast_dismiss()` to clear all.

## Dynamic UI and modules

Components self-initialize, so overlays and inputs rendered inside `renderUI()`
work without manual re-binding:

```{r}
output$panel <- renderUI({
  shad_dialog("dyn", trigger = shad_button("Open"),
              title = "Rendered on demand", shad_p("Hello."))
})
```

All `inputId`s pass through `session$ns()`, so components and their
`update_shad_*()` / `shad_*_open()` helpers are safe inside Shiny modules — use
the same bare id in UI and server as you would with base inputs.
